title: k8s-node-provisioning-debug-breadcrumbs-alex
content:
Context:
- Working on recurring incidents where new worker nodes in the EKS/GKE-like managed clusters become NotReady or never fully join the cluster after bootstrap. This is a personal scratchpad of commands tried, outputs, error snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

Timeline / quick notes:
- 2024-10-01: First noticed spike of NotReady nodes after a deploy of the custom cloud-init image.
- 2024-10-02: Rolled back image -> fewer failures but still intermittent.
- 2024-10-03: Started live debugging on a repro instance.

Commands tried (raw):
1) Basic cluster view
$ kubectl get nodes -o wide
# Output snippet (typical failing node)
NAME                           STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION   INTERNAL-IP    EXTERNAL-IP   OS-IMAGE             KERNEL-VERSION
ip-10-0-7-234.ec2.internal     NotReady   <none>   4m    v1.25.10  10.0.7.234     <none>        Ubuntu 22.04.2 LTS    5.15.0-76-generic

2) Describe node to see conditions / events
$ kubectl describe node ip-10-0-7-234.ec2.internal
# Key bits from Events/Conditions:
- Conditions: Ready=False (Reason: KubeletNotReady)
- Conditions: NetworkUnavailable=True (Reason: CalicoIsNotReady)
- Events: Failed to update status for node: timed out waiting for the condition
- Events: taint/csi-attacher... (noise)

3) Check kubelet journal (ssh into node)
$ sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager
# Relevant errors:
Oct 03 11:12:05 ip-10-0-7-234 kubelet[2345]: E1003 11:12:05.123456    2345 kubelet_node_status.go:265] Unable to register node "ip-10-0-7-234.ec2.internal": node "ip-10-0-7-234.ec2.internal" not found
Oct 03 11:12:06 ip-10-0-7-234 kubelet[2345]: E1003 11:12:06.123457    2345 kubelet.go:2476] node object has no finalizers, skipping API call
Oct 03 11:12:07 ip-10-0-7-234 kubelet[2345]: W1003 11:12:07.123458    2345 kubelet_node_status.go:123] Failed to update status: Post "https://api.cluster.local/api/v1/nodes/ip-10-0-7-234.ec2.internal/status": net/http: TLS handshake timeout

4) Check container runtime and cni
$ sudo crictl ps -a
# containerd responds but pause containers not present for pod infra in some cases
$ sudo systemctl status containerd
# containerd active. But found repeated image pull backoff for calico/node

5) Helm / CNI checks (from control plane):
$ kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=calico-node -o wide
# Some calico-node pods Pending on new nodes, reason: CrashLoopBackOff or ImagePullBackOff

6) kube-proxy logs on new node
$ kubectl logs -n kube-system kube-proxy-ip-10-0-7-234 -c kube-proxy
# Output shows iptables module errors: failed to set chain, permission denied (we run with hostNetwork true)

Observed error patterns / snippets:
- "Unable to register node \"...\": node \"...\" not found" (kubelet)
- "TLS handshake timeout" when kubelet posts status (intermittent, 5-10s timeouts)
- "NetworkUnavailable: True (CalicoIsNotReady)" on nodes that otherwise have containerd up
- ImagePullBackOff for calico/node or cilium images on some AZs (private subnet egress restrictions?)
- cloud-init logs show: Could not reach metadata service at 169.254.169.254 for IAM role retrieval (this was for older repro)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Bootstrapping race: kubelet registers before CNI finished -> node status flips to NotReady and events cascade. But this shouldn't block registration entirely.
2) Network egress / image registry access failing in some AZs -> CNI daemonset pods fail to start -> NetworkUnavailable stays True. Root cause may be a VPC egress/NAT/GW config (we saw ImagePullBackOff).
3) TLS handshake timeout suggests control plane API endpoint intermittently unreachable from node (DNS or ENI route table issues). Could be SG/Route misconfig on newly provisioned ENIs.
4) cloud-init / userdata script race: kubelet service starts before node labels/tags/iam creds available; kubelet attempts registration and hits "node not found" because apiserver expects specific cloud provider annotation/metadata that isn't applied yet.
5) container runtime misconfig (containerd misconfigured with incorrect registry mirror) causing pod infra to not start fast enough.

Things I modified / tested:
- Increased kubelet start delay in cloud-init (systemd drop-in) to 30s -> reduced frequency but did not eliminate failures.
- Toggled image pull credentials / added egress route for restricted AZ -> calico pods started more reliably in that AZ for 6/8 nodes.
- Temporarily added sleep 60s before kubeadm join in bootstrap -> similar improvement to start delay.
- For a repro node, manually pulled calico image and started calico/node manifest -> node transitioned to Ready. This strongly suggests image/CNI availability timing is a primary factor.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Helm: increased calico daemonset pod priorityClass and set tolerations to allow immediate scheduling on new nodes. (PR: infra#412)
- Autoscaler: slowed scale-up to give extra time for bootstrap (k8s-cluster autoscaler flags adjusted).

Remaining open questions / experiments to run:
- Reproduce deterministic failure: create tiny proxy to simulate slow image registry and confirm node remains NotReady until CNI ready.
- Collect packet captures/delve into ENI route config on failed node during TLS handshake timeouts (is control plane endpoint IP reachable?).
- Check kube-apiserver logs for any rejected registration requests around the timestamp (authz, admission plugins?).
- Verify node annotations expected by cloud-controller-manager / kubelet in our cloud provider integration (do we expect certain tags present before join?).

Concrete next steps (todo):
- [ ] Add verbose kubelet logs to repro nodes (Kubelet extra args: --v=4) and capture full kubelet/journal during bootstrap.
- [ ] Add automated smoke test in cluster-provisioner that waits for CNI DaemonSet pods to be Ready on newly created nodes before marking node join complete.
- [ ] Run a controlled repro with egress blocked in one AZ and collect timelines (cloud-init, kubelet, cni start times).
- [ ] Validate that our AMI's containerd config includes correct registry mirrors and that credentials are accessible at boot.
- [ ] Follow up on infra#412 (helm calico priority) to consider keeping as mitigation or reverting after root cause fixed.

Notes to self / random CLI snippets I used:
- kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 50
- ssh ubuntu@ip-10-0-7-234 sudo journalctl -u kubelet -f
- ssh ubuntu@ip-10-0-7-234 sudo crictl pull docker.io/calico/node:v3.24.0
- curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://api.cluster.local:6443/healthz || echo "apiserver unreachable"
- curl -v http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/ || echo "meta unreachable"

If stuck: ping Jordan/Kim or Priya for infra-networking deep dive. Also check recent cloud infra change timeline in #infra-changes slack thread.

End of scratchpad.
